description: Tool to manage a series of patches.

next.name: add
tip: Add one or more files to the topmost or named patch.
Files must be added to the patch before being modified.
Files that are modified by patches already applied on top of the specified patch cannot be added.

option.name: -P
tip: Patch to add files to.

next.name: annotate
tip: Print an annotated listing of the specified file showing which patches modify which lines.
Only applied patches are included.

option.name: -P
tip: Stop checking for changes at the specified patch rather than the topmost patch.

next.name: applied
tip: Print a list of applied patches, or all patches up to and including the specified patch in the file series.

next.name: delete
tip: Remove the specified or topmost patch from the series file.
If the patch is applied, quilt will attempt to remove it first.
Only the topmost patch can be removed right now.

option.name: --backup
tip: Rename the patch file to patch~ rather than deleting it.
Ignored if not used with -r.

option.name: -n
tip: Delete the next patch after topmost, rather than the specified or topmost patch.

option.name: -r
tip: Remove the deleted patch file from the patches directory as well.

next.name: diff
tip: Produces a diff of the specified file(s) in the topmost or specified patch.
If no files are specified, all files that are modified are included.

option.name: --color
tip: Use syntax coloring (auto activates it only if the output is a tty).
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: always, auto, never.

option.name: --combine
tip: Create a combined diff for all patches between this patch and the patch specified with -P.
A patch name of - is equivalent to specifying the first applied patch.
Use the first applied patch.

option.name: --diff
tip: Use the specified utility for generating the diff.
The utility is invoked with the original and new file name as arguments.

option.name: --no-index
tip: Do not output Index: lines.

option.name: --no-timestamps
tip: Do not include file timestamps in patch headers.

option.name: --snapshot
tip: Diff against the snapshot created by quilt snapshot.

option.name: --sort
tip: Sort files by their name instead of preserving the original order.

option.name: -c
tip: Create a context diff with 3 lines of context.

option.name: -C
tip: Create a context diff with the given number of context lines.

option.name: -p
tip: Create a -p n style patch (-p0 or -p1 are supported).
Use ab to create a -p1 style patch with a/file and b/file as the original and new filenames instead of the default dir.orig/file and dir/file names.

option.name: -P
tip: Create a diff for the specified patch. (default topmost patch)

option.name: -R
tip: Create a reverse diff.

option.name: -u
tip: Create a unified diff with 3 lines of context.

option.name: -U
tip: Create a unified diff with the given number of context lines.

option.name: -z
tip: Write to standard output the changes that have been made relative to the topmost or specified patch.

next.name: edit
tip: Edit the specified file(s) in $EDITOR (vi) after adding it (them) to the topmost patch.

next.name: files
tip: Print the list of files that the topmost or specified patch changes.

option.name: --combine
tip: Create a listing for all patches between this patch and the topmost or specified patch.
A patch name of - is equivalent to specifying the first applied patch.
Use the first applied patch.

option.name: -a
tip: List all files in all applied patches.

option.name: -l
tip: Add patch name to output.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose, more user friendly output.

next.name: fold
tip: Integrate the patch read from standard input into the topmost patch.
After making sure that all files modified are part of the topmost patch, the patch is applied with the specified strip level (which defaults to 1).

option.name: -f
tip: Force apply, even if the patch has rejects.
Unless in quiet mode, apply the patch interactively: the patch utility may ask questions.

option.name: -p
tip: The number of pathname components to strip from file names when applying patchfile.

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet operation.

option.name: -R
tip: Apply patch in reverse.

next.name: fork
tip: Fork the topmost patch.
Forking a patch means creating a verbatim copy of it under a new name, and use that new name instead of the original one in the current series.
This is useful when a patch has to be modified, but the original version should be preserved.
If new_name is missing, the name of the forked patch is the current patch name followed by -2; a trailing dash-and-number is incremented.

next.name: graph
tip: Generate a dot(1) directed graph showing the dependencies between applied patches.
A patch depends on another patch if both touch the same file or, with the --lines option, if their modifications overlap.
Unless otherwise specified, the graph includes all patches that the topmost patch depends on.
When a patch name is specified, create a graph for that patch instead of the topmost one.

option.name: --all
tip: Generate a graph including all applied patches and their dependencies.
Unapplied patches are not included.

option.name: --edge-labels
tip: Label graph edges with the file names that the adjacent patches modify.
Possible values: files.

option.name: --lines
tip: Compute dependencies by looking at the lines the patches modify.
Unless a different num is specified, two lines of context are included.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --reduce
tip: Eliminate transitive edges from the graph.

option.name: -T
tip: Directly produce a PostScript output file.
The format is passed to dot(1) -T.

next.name: grep
tip: Grep through the source files, recursively, skipping patches and quilt meta-information.
If no filename argument is given, the whole source tree is searched.
Options other than -h are passed to grep(1).
The grep -h option can be passed after --; a pattern starting with a dash can be passed after -- --.

next.name: header
tip: Print or change the header of the topmost or specified patch.

option.name: --backup
tip: Create a backup copy of the old version of a patch as patch~.

option.name: --strip-diffstat
tip: Strip diffstat output from the header.

option.name: --strip-trailing-whitespace
tip: Strip trailing whitespace at the end of lines of the header.

option.name: -a
tip: Append to the existing patch header.

option.name: -e
tip: Edit the header in $EDITOR (vi).

option.name: -r
tip: Replace the existing patch header.

next.name: import
tip: Import external patches.
The patches will be inserted following the current top patch, and must be pushed after import to apply them.

option.name: -d
tip: When overwriting in existing patch, keep the old (o), all (a), or new (n) patch header.
If both patches include headers, this option must be specified.
This option is only effective when -f is used.
Possible values: o, a, n.

option.name: -f
tip: Overwrite/update existing patches.

option.name: -p
tip: Number of directory levels to strip when applying. (default 1)

option.name: -P
tip: Patch filename to use inside quilt.
This option can only be used when importing a single patch.

option.name: -R
tip: Apply patch in reverse.

next.name: mail
tip: Create mail messages from a specified range of patches, or all patches in the series file.
Store them in a mailbox file, or send them immediately.
The editor is opened with a template for the introduction.
When specifying a range, a first patch name of - denotes the first, and a last patch name of - denotes the last patch in the series.

option.name: --bcc
tip: Append a recipient to the Bcc header.

option.name: --cc
tip: Append a recipient to the Cc header.

option.name: --charset
tip: Specify a particular message encoding on systems which don't use UTF-8 or ISO-8859-15.
This character encoding must match the one used in the patches.

option.name: --from
tip: The value for the From header to use.
If no --from option is given, the value of the --sender option is used.

option.name: --mbox
tip: Store all messages in the specified file in mbox format.
The mbox can later be sent using formail, for example.

option.name: --prefix
tip: Use an alternate prefix in the bracketed part of the subjects generated. (default patch)

option.name: --reply-to
tip: Add the appropriate headers to reply to the specified message.

option.name: --send
tip: Send the messages directly.

option.name: --sender
tip: The envelope sender address to use.
The address must be of the form user@domain.name.
No display name is allowed.

option.name: --signature
tip: Append the specified signature to messages.
Defaults to ~/.signature if found; use - for no signature.
Do not append a signature.

option.name: --subject
tip: The value for the Subject header to use.

option.name: --to
tip: Append a recipient to the To header.

option.name: -m
tip: Text to use as the text in the introduction.
When this option is used, the editor will not be invoked, and the patches will be processed immediately.

option.name: -M
tip: Like -m, but read the introduction from file.

next.name: new
tip: Create a new patch with the specified file name, and insert it after the topmost patch.
The name can be prefixed with a sub-directory name, allowing for grouping related patches together.

option.name: -p
tip: Create a -p n style patch (-p0 or -p1 are supported).

next.name: next
tip: Print the name of the next patch after the specified or topmost patch in the series file.

next.name: patches
tip: Print the list of patches that modify any of the specified files.
Uses a heuristic to determine which files are modified by unapplied patches.
Note that this heuristic is much slower than scanning applied patches.

option.name: --color
tip: Use syntax coloring (auto activates it only if the output is a tty).
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: always, auto, never.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose, more user friendly output.

next.name: pop
tip: Remove patch(es) from the stack of applied patches.
Without options, the topmost patch is removed.
When a number is specified, remove the specified number of patches.
When a patch name is specified, remove patches until the specified patch ends up on top of the stack.
Patch names may include the patches/ prefix.

option.name: --refresh
tip: Automatically refresh every patch before it gets unapplied.

option.name: -a
tip: Remove all applied patches.

option.name: -f
tip: Force remove.
The state before the patch(es) were applied will be restored from backup files.

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet operation.

option.name: -R
tip: Always verify if the patch removes cleanly; don't rely on timestamp checks.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose operation.

next.name: previous
tip: Print the name of the previous patch before the specified or topmost patch in the series file.

next.name: push
tip: Apply patch(es) from the series file.
Without options, the next patch in the series file is applied.
When a number is specified, apply the specified number of patches.
When a patch name is specified, apply all patches up to and including the specified patch.
Patch names may include the patches/ prefix.

option.name: --color
tip: Use syntax coloring (auto activates it only if the output is a tty).
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: always, auto, never.

option.name: --fuzz
tip: Set the maximum fuzz factor. (default 2)

option.name: --leave-rejects
tip: Leave around the reject files patch produced, even if the patch is not actually applied.

option.name: --merge
tip: Merge the patch file into the original files (see patch(1)).
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: merge, diff3.

option.name: --refresh
tip: Automatically refresh every patch after it was successfully applied.

option.name: -a
tip: Apply all patches in the series file.

option.name: -f
tip: Force apply, even if the patch has rejects.

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet operation.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose operation.

next.name: refresh
tip: Refreshes the specified patch, or the topmost patch by default.
Documentation that comes before the actual patch in the patch file is retained.
It is possible to refresh patches that are not on top.
If any patches on top of the patch to refresh modify the same files, the script aborts by default.
Patches can still be refreshed with -f; a warning is printed for each shadowed file, and changes by more recent patches are ignored.

option.name: --backup
tip: Create a backup copy of the old version of a patch as patch~.

option.name: --diffstat
tip: Add a diffstat section to the patch header, or replace the existing diffstat section.

option.name: --no-index
tip: Do not output Index: lines.

option.name: --no-timestamps
tip: Do not include file timestamps in patch headers.

option.name: --sort
tip: Sort files by their name instead of preserving the original order.

option.name: --strip-trailing-whitespace
tip: Strip trailing whitespace at the end of lines.

option.name: -c
tip: Create a context diff with 3 lines of context.

option.name: -C
tip: Create a context diff with the given number of context lines.

option.name: -f
tip: Enforce refreshing of a patch that is not on top.

option.name: -p
tip: Create a -p n style patch (-p0 or -p1 are supported).
Use ab to create a -p1 style patch with a/file and b/file as the original and new filenames instead of the default dir.orig/file and dir/file names.

option.name: -u
tip: Create a unified diff with 3 lines of context.

option.name: -U
tip: Create a unified diff with the given number of context lines.

option.name: -z
tip: Create a new patch containing the changes instead of refreshing the topmost patch.
If no new name is specified, -2 is added to the original patch name, etc.
The new name must be attached, e.g. -znew_name.

next.name: remove
tip: Remove one or more files from the topmost or named patch.
Files that are modified by patches on top of the specified patch cannot be removed.

option.name: -P
tip: Remove named files from the named patch.

next.name: rename
tip: Rename the topmost or named patch.

option.name: -P
tip: Patch to rename.

next.name: revert
tip: Revert uncommitted changes to the topmost or named patch for the specified file(s).
After the revert, quilt diff -z will show no differences for those files.
Changes to files that are modified by patches on top of the specified patch cannot be reverted.

option.name: -P
tip: Revert changes in the named patch.

next.name: series
tip: Print the names of all patches in the series file.

option.name: --color
tip: Use syntax coloring (auto activates it only if the output is a tty).
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: always, auto, never.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose, more user friendly output.

next.name: setup
tip: Initializes a source tree from an rpm spec file or a quilt series file.
The setup command is only guaranteed to work properly on spec files where applying all the patches is the last thing done in the %prep section.

option.name: --fast
tip: Use the new, faster method to process the spec file.
In this mode, rpmbuild is told to generate a working tree directly in the target directory.
This is the default since quilt 0.67.

option.name: --fuzz
tip: Set the maximum fuzz factor (needs rpm 4.6 or later).

option.name: --slow
tip: Use the original, slow method to process the spec file.
In this mode, rpmbuild generates a working tree in a temporary directory while all its actions are recorded, and then everything is replayed from scratch in the target directory.

option.name: --sourcedir
tip: Directory that contains the package sources. (default .)

option.name: --spec-filter
tip: Before passing the spec file to rpmbuild, apply a filter to it.
FILTER must be an executable script which reads the original spec file from stdin and writes the filtered spec file to stdout.
FILTER can be a path to a custom script, or a simple name referencing one of the filter scripts shipped with quilt.

option.name: -d
tip: Optional path prefix for the resulting source tree.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose debug output.

next.name: snapshot
tip: Take a snapshot of the current working state.
After taking the snapshot, the tree can be modified in the usual ways, including pushing and popping patches.
A diff against the tree at the moment of the snapshot can be generated with quilt diff --snapshot.

option.name: -d
tip: Only remove current snapshot.

next.name: top
tip: Print the name of the topmost patch on the current stack of applied patches.

next.name: unapplied
tip: Print a list of patches that are not applied, or all patches that follow the specified patch in the series file.

next.name: upgrade
tip: Upgrade the meta-data in a working tree from an old version of quilt to the current version.
This command is only needed when the quilt meta-data format has changed, and the working tree still contains old-format meta-data.

option.name: --version
tip: Print the version number and exit immediately.

global_option.name: --quiltrc
tip: Use the specified configuration file instead of ~/.quiltrc.
Use - to read no configuration file.
Read no configuration file.

global_option.name: --trace
tip: Runs the command in bash trace mode (-x).
For internal debugging.
The value must be attached with =.
Possible values: verbose.

global_option.name: -h
tip: Print help.
